domain_label: Turlock Independent Ag & Specialty — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent Ag & Specialty format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its B2B-versus-consumer demand engine, equipment/fleet and licensed-labor model, the CSLB/Veterinary-Board/CDFA/Cottage-Food licensing gate, cost structure and labeled benchmark margins, supplier chain, and the operating decisions that make the format viable or doom it — without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate scaled by an observable size signal (firm age, division count, multi-vet vs single-vet, format), tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business such as Lander, TDR or Stanislaus Farm Supply

the universe is the 14 verified independent Ag & Specialty businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json (chains excluded), in a town of ~72,919 whose B2B demand unit is the county herd and planted acreage, not residents

city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, ~$3.15B county ag value, ~132 dairies, license fees, CFO caps) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented

supplier-to-named-business links (OEM dealer affiliations, animal-health distributors) are representative inference about the realistic supply universe, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship
cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (AVMA/iVET360, IBISWorld, NBDA, cooperative ag-retail norms, BLS wages) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: chain and franchise operations such as Tractor Supply or big-box dealer networks (the catalog is independents only)
stating any actual dollar revenue, profit, or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the sizing detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
small-animal/companion veterinary, general retail, and household services except where an Ag & Specialty format straddles into a consumer arm (e.g. Turlock Feed's western-wear apparel tag)
tax, legal, and regulatory advice for an individual operator; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing or contractor-board application

competency_questions.question: Why does one sector label hide two different economies, and what demand unit drives each?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SECTOR_TWO_ECONOMIES names the essential herd/acre-scaled B2B spine (ag equipment, feed, large-animal vet) against the thin-demand discretionary consumer edge (bike, music, cottage-food) and HERD_NOT_HEADCOUNT states that the B2B demand unit is the county herd, not city residents

competency_questions.question: Why does a 73k town sustain three each of vet, equipment and feed formats, and what caps the count from going higher?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DAIRY_ALMOND_BASE establishes the ~$3.15B / ~132-dairy base as the expander that lifts the B2B count, and SATURATION_WHITESPACE gives the per-format saturation read against the correct denominator and where the count is at-ceiling versus under-saturated

competency_questions.question: How are per-format revenue and margin bands estimated honestly when no per-business revenue is public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_ESTIMATE_METHOD states the published-benchmark-times-observable-size-signal method, the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level and a confirmation path, and COST_STRUCTURE_BACKBONE supplies the COGS/labor/net backbone it scales

competency_questions.question: What licensing must a pump/dairy-construction firm, a large-animal vet, a feed retailer and a cottage-food producer each clear before operating?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_LICENSING_GATES states the CSLB C-57/C-61, Veterinary Medical Board premises + DEA mobility, CDFA feed/fertilizer licensing, and Cottage-Food Class A/B caps with public sources and identifies which is the binding entry gate per format

competency_questions.question: Why is scarce licensed/skilled labor, not customer demand, the binding cap on growing the B2B lines?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABOR_SCARCITY_CAP explains that only ~1.3% of US vets do food-animal work (~52 hr/week) and that the rural pump-tech/welder/electrician pool is tight, and names the founder-succession risk at firms like Sallaberry (since 1968) and TDR (since 1972)

competency_questions.question: What is the real Central Valley proximity advantage and which suppliers form the realistic supply universe per format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLY_CHAIN_GATES names the milking-system OEMs (DeLaval, GEA, BouMatic), feed mills/cooperative buying (Stanislaus FS via Valley Wide), animal-health distributors (Patterson/MWI/Covetrus) and QBP/instrument-OEM nodes per format, flagged as representative inference, and quantifies the short-freight/dealer-proximity edge

competency_questions.question: What does it take to run the ag-equipment/dairy-systems line, and why is its revenue band the widest and lowest-confidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AG_EQUIPMENT_MODEL describes the owner-led skilled-trade plus capital-projects model (Sallaberry pumps, TDR full dairy design/build), the parts+service+project revenue mix, and ties the band width to the project-mix swing and the CSLB/labor gate

competency_questions.question: Why is feed/farm supply the thinnest-margin B2B line and how does cooperative scale or service revenue save it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FEED_FARMSUPPLY_MODEL states the ~70-80% commodity COGS and ~2-6% net, the cooperative buying lever (Stanislaus FS via Valley Wide) versus the small-store service differentiation (Turlock Feed's sharpening/tack, Elite's counter), and the under-saturation read against the herd base

competency_questions.question: Why is the large-animal/dairy vet the labor-bound professional-service model and how do productized lab divisions lift its band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LARGE_ANIMAL_VET_MODEL gives the ambulatory dispatch model, the high (~35-50%) licensed-DVM labor share, the productized divisions (Lander's Quality Milk Service, Dairy Diagnostics, OPU/Embryo Transfer), the per-vet benchmark scaled by DVM count, and the high-gross-thin-net caveat

competency_questions.question: How do the consumer-edge music and bike formats survive against contracting categories and Modesto/online leakage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MUSIC_INSTRUMENTS_MODEL names the recurring channels (Hendrickson's school-band+piano, Dale's lessons/repair, Ingram's rental fleet) and BIKE_SHOP_MODEL names the service-anchored single-store equilibrium (Cycle Masters since 1978, free tire changes), each tied to the LEAKAGE_RULE moat

competency_questions.question: Why is the cottage-food/farm-stand format structurally capped rather than demand-capped, and where does the CFO ceiling not bind?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COTTAGE_FARMSTAND_MODEL states the self-supplied seasonal producer model (Cipponeri honey/dried fruit/stone fruit), the Class A/B CFO caps (~$86,206 / ~$172,411) on the processed slice only, and that honey and whole produce fall outside CFO so the stand as a whole is seasonality-limited

competency_questions.question: Given demand, cost, licensing and saturation, what is the merged go/no-go on entering a given Ag & Specialty format, and why is the B2B half a correlated bet?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTRY_GO_NOGO composes saturation, cost/licensing gate and demand against the correct denominator into a defensible verdict (B2B demand-open but gate-locked; consumer gate-open but demand-locked), and CORRELATED_HERD_RISK flags that vet/feed/equipment are one dairy-cycle bet, not diversified

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per veterinarian, per farm-supply store, per shop) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, never a reported or claimed actual revenue for any named business such as Lander, TDR or Cipponeri.

The rule that the B2B half of the sector (ag equipment, feed, large-animal vet) is sized against the county herd (~132 dairies) and planted acreage, not the ~72,919 city residents; per-resident saturation math is the wrong denominator for these lines.

An observable proxy (firm age, division count, multi-vet versus single-vet, capital-projects versus pump-repair format) used to scale a published per-unit benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual sales.

The principle that the shippable, price-comparable, non-urgent dollar leaks to Modesto big-box and online (Amazon, Chewy, Sweetwater, Tractor Supply), while the urgent, fitted, serviced, or herd-side dollar stays local; the survival logic of every durable independent here.

The large-animal vet operating model in which veterinarians drive to herds and the clinic is a dispatch base; fleet capex and rolling truck stock with cold chain replace storefront retail, and operations are dispatch- and emergency-driven, not storefront-hours.

The lever by which a feed/farm-supply retailer reaches competitive COGS on low-margin commodity feed; Stanislaus Farm Supply merged into Valley Wide Cooperative for exactly this purchasing scale, a documented structural fact that small counter stores cannot match.

The California State License Board contractor classes that gate pump/well and dairy-construction work — C-57 Well Drilling (required when labor+materials exceed $500), commonly paired with C-61/D-21 Machinery & Pumps, plus general/structural classes for parlor builds — a binding entry barrier for the ag-equipment line.

The California Cottage Food Operation statutory gross-sales ceiling on the home-processed slice — ~$86,206 Class A (county registration, direct sales) / ~$172,411 Class B (permit + annual kitchen inspection, adds wholesale), 2025 inflation-adjusted — which bounds only the regulated processed line, not honey or whole produce.

The dominant sector risk that vet, equipment and feed demand all derive from the same Stanislaus dairy/almond cash flow, so a milk-price downturn or herd shock (e.g. the 2024 avian-influenza quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies) compresses four of six sub-categories at once — correlated, not diversified, exposure.

The honesty rule that the verified count of 14 independents is a floor, not a ceiling: it is the minimum confirmed via public sources, and additional micro-producers and very small feed/tack shops plausibly exist below the listing-visibility threshold and would only raise the count.

nodes.definition: Establish the structural fact that the Ag & Specialty label hides two economies. Economy A is the B2B ag spine — Ag Equipment & Repair (Sallaberry, TDR, The Dairy Solutions Group), Feed/Farm Supply (Stanislaus Farm Supply, Turlock Feed, Elite), and Large-Animal/Dairy Vet (Azores, Lander, Mid Valley) — selling essential, non-discretionary, herd/acre-scaled services to commercial operators on cash/net terms, not insurance. Economy B is the thin-demand discretionary consumer edge — Bike Shop (Cycle Masters), Music/Instruments (Hendrickson's, Dale's, Ingram's), and the Cottage-Food/Farm Stand producer (Cipponeri) — selling to households and highly leakage-prone. Every downstream format judgment must first place the format in the correct economy because the demand unit, payment model and saturation denominator differ completely between them.

included: the B2B spine vs consumer edge split
the six sub-categories assigned to each economy
the cash/net-terms vs household-discretionary payment difference

pros.claim: Splitting the sector into two economies stops a single saturation or demand rule from being mis-applied across formats with opposite logic
pros.example: reading three vet practices against the county herd while reading the bike shop against city residents

cons.claim: The clean split blurs at the straddles, which can be over-stated as a hard wall
cons.example: Stanislaus Farm Supply carrying an ag-equipment secondary tag and Turlock Feed an apparel tag cross the B2B/consumer line

failure_modes: applying a per-resident saturation read to a B2B herd-scaled line
treating the two economies as equally discretionary when only the consumer edge is
acceptance_tests: the analysis assigns each of the six sub-categories to Economy A (B2B spine) or Economy B (consumer edge) and states the demand unit and payment model for each
revisit_triggers: a new sub-category enters the catalog
a straddle business reclassifies its primary category
the dairy base shifts enough to change a B2B line's demand logic

base.update_signal: a sub-category, straddle, or demand-unit assignment changes

nodes.definition: Quantify the demand base that drives the whole B2B spine: Stanislaus County's 2024 gross agricultural value was ~$3.15B (almonds ~$825M, milk ~$755M) anchored by ~132 commercial dairies, all cited public facts from the 2024 Crop Report. This base, not the ~72,919 residents, is why a 73k town carries three large-animal vets, three ag-equipment firms and three feed outlets — a generic same-size town with no dairy cluster would carry a fraction. At ~44 dairies per vet practice (derived 132 divided by 3) the three vets are matched to herd load, not over-built. The base is also the expander whose health every B2B format is hostage to, which CORRELATED_HERD_RISK later turns into the sector's dominant downside.

included: ~$3.15B county ag value and ~132-dairy count with sources
the base as the B2B count expander
the ~44-dairies-per-vet derivation

pros.claim: Grounding the B2B count in the cited county ag base explains why the count is high without invoking population
pros.example: three vet practices matched to ~132 dairies at ~44 dairies each read as well-matched, not oversupplied

cons.claim: A point-in-time county value can be read as stable when it is volatile and recovering from a 2024 shock
cons.example: treating ~$3.15B as a fixed floor while 2024 saw a ~6% county ag-value decline

failure_modes: citing the county value as current when it is a year-stamped 2024 figure
deriving per-vet ratios as precise when DVM counts per practice are unknown
acceptance_tests: the base cites the ~$3.15B county ag value, the ~132-dairy count and the ~44-dairies-per-vet derivation, all year-stamped and sourced
revisit_triggers: a new Stanislaus County Crop Report is published
the dairy count or county ag value shifts materially
a milk- or almond-price cycle moves the base

base.update_signal: a county ag value, dairy count, or commodity-price figure is updated

nodes.definition: Establish the denominator rule that governs every B2B saturation read: city per-capita is the wrong measure for ag-equipment, feed and large-animal vet, whose true market is the county herd and planted acreage, not the ~72,919 residents. The naive per-10k read (3 outlets divided by 72,919 times 10,000 equals 0.41 per 10k) makes feed look at-market against an IBISWorld ~0.57 per 10k norm, but read against ~132 dairies plus thousands of acres the three feed outlets are thin, not crowded. The consumer edge (bike, music) is the one half where the per-resident denominator is correct. Mis-choosing the denominator is the single most common saturation error in this sector.

included: the herd/acre denominator for B2B lines
the per-resident denominator for the consumer edge
the worked per-10k example showing the error

pros.claim: Pinning the correct denominator per line prevents the headline per-10k read from mislabeling under-saturated B2B lines as at-market
pros.example: feed reading thin against ~132 dairies despite a 0.41-per-10k city figure near the national norm

cons.claim: The herd denominator is harder to size precisely than population, so B2B saturation reads carry more uncertainty
cons.example: acreage and herd-load per outlet are estimates, not a clean per-capita count

failure_modes: reading a B2B line against city residents and declaring it saturated
applying the herd denominator to the genuinely population-scaled bike and music lines
acceptance_tests: the rule states the herd/acre denominator for the three B2B lines and the per-resident denominator for the consumer edge, with the worked per-10k example
revisit_triggers: the herd or acreage base is re-counted
a B2B line's true market unit changes
a per-format saturation read is challenged on its denominator

base.update_signal: a herd/acre count or a line's market-unit assignment changes

nodes.definition: Account for the demand cap on the consumer edge: a 73k town generates only so many bike and instrument purchases, and Modesto (~20 min north, ~218k) plus online (Amazon, Chewy, Tractor Supply.com, Sweetwater, Guitar Center) siphon the shippable, price-comparable, non-urgent dollar. The leakage rule is the survival logic of the whole sector: the shippable dollar leaks out, the urgent, fitted, serviced, or herd-side dollar stays local. It holds bike at a one-store equilibrium (a nationally contracting category, ~6,195 to ~3,600 US shops 2000-2022) and makes three music stores viable only via captive school-band/CSU recurring revenue. Any consumer-edge judgment that ignores leakage will over-state Turlock headroom.

included: Modesto and online leakage on the consumer edge
the shippable-leaks vs serviced-stays rule
the bike one-store and music recurring-revenue equilibria

pros.claim: Naming the leakage rule explains why the consumer edge survives on service and relationships rather than price-comparable sales
pros.example: Cycle Masters bundling free tire changes to hold the urgent/serviced dollar the internet cannot ship

cons.claim: Leakage is a behavioral estimate, not a measured flow, so it can be over- or under-applied
cons.example: assuming all instrument spend leaks while the school-band rental channel stays captive locally

failure_modes: applying leakage to herd-captive B2B lines that do not cross-shop
treating leakage as measured when it is a behavioral estimate
acceptance_tests: the rule states the shippable-leaks vs serviced-stays principle, names Modesto and the online channels, and applies it to the bike and music equilibria
revisit_triggers: a big-box or dealer development opens in Modesto
an online channel materially changes ag/instrument retail
a measured leakage study is produced

base.update_signal: regional big-box supply or online retail share shifts

nodes.definition: Anchor each Ag & Specialty line to its published, cited margin skeleton — drugs-versus-labor for vets, parts-versus-trades for equipment, commodity-COGS for feed — so a revenue band becomes a margin reality, all labeled estimates: Large-Animal Vet COGS ~25-40% drugs/consumables, labor high ~35-50% on licensed DVM/RVT, net ~10-18%; Ag Equipment & Repair parts ~40-55% on service (higher on capital projects), trades labor ~25-35%, net ~8-15%; Feed/Farm Supply commodity COGS high ~70-80%, labor ~10-18%, net ~2-6%; Music/Instruments ~40-60% on instrument resale (far lower on lessons/repair), labor ~20-30%, net ~5-12%; Bike Shop goods ~50-60% (NBDA ~49.7% gross on goods), labor ~15-25%, net ~5-10%; Cottage-Food self-supplied with capped CFO gross. These are sector-typical planning priors from AVMA/iVET360, IBISWorld, NBDA and cooperative norms, not audited books, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality.

included: COGS/labor/net benchmark ranges by sub-category
the planning-prior status of the figures
the sources behind each band

pros.claim: Pairing every revenue band with its COGS/labor/net backbone stops high gross from being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: a feed retailer booking high commodity revenue still netting only ~2-6% on ~70-80% COGS

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away cooperative scale and project-mix swings that move real Turlock margins
cons.example: the ag-equipment band swinging with a parlor build versus a pump repair the benchmark cannot capture

failure_modes: importing a national benchmark without adjusting for cooperative scale or project mix
reading a benchmark range as a single point estimate
acceptance_tests: COGS, labor and net benchmark ranges are stated by sub-category with sources and labeled as planning priors
revisit_triggers: a new AVMA/IBISWorld/NBDA benchmark guide is published
wage or commodity inflation shifts a labor or COGS share
a cooperative-pricing change moves the feed band

base.update_signal: a published cost-structure benchmark or commodity/wage figure is revised

nodes.definition: Set the per-veterinarian-and-per-store scaling rule that turns a herd/firm-size signal into an honest revenue band when no privately-held Ag operator discloses sales: take a published industry benchmark (~$250k-$375k per veterinarian; US farm-supply per-store band; small/medium music-shop band; single-store NBDA bike norm) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (firm age, division count, multi-vet versus single-vet, capital-projects versus pump-repair format), then tag the result estimate-not-actual, assign a confidence level, and name the confirmation path (DVM count per practice, division count, format observation). The resulting per-operator bands — vet ~$0.75M-$3M, ag equipment ~$0.5M-$5M+, feed ~$0.5M-$3M, music ~$0.25M-$0.75M, bike ~$0.3M-$0.8M, cottage-food <$50k-$150k — are planning estimates, never claims about a named business such as Lander or TDR.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal method
the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
the six per-operator bands
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a multi-vet practice at ~$250k-$375k per DVM scaling to a band tagged estimate with a DVM-count confirmation path

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the size signal is mis-observed or the confidence label is dropped
cons.example: treating the ag-equipment band as precise when project mix and DVM/crew counts are unknown

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
scaling by a mis-observed size signal and reporting a false precision
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level, the size signal used, and a named confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published per-vet/per-store benchmark is updated
a confirming size signal (DVM count, division count) becomes available
a format's observable size signal changes

base.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of a confirming count changes

nodes.definition: Encode the binding honesty rule as its own node so it cannot be skipped: no per-business dollar revenue, profit or owner income is ever stated as fact for any named Turlock business, because none is public for these privately held independents. Every dollar figure tied to a sub-category is a labeled benchmark estimate carrying its method (benchmark times size signal), its public source, and a confidence level, and the word estimate travels with it. Where a high gross band exists it is paired with the thin-net caveat so high revenue is never mistaken for high profit. A request to state a named business's actual revenue must be refused and answered only with a labeled estimate plus its confirmation path.

included: the no-actual-dollar-as-fact rule
method + source + confidence travelling with every number
the high-gross-thin-net pairing and the refusal behavior
excluded: the supplier-link inference rule (separate honesty node)

pros.claim: Making the honesty rule a first-class node guarantees every band is labeled at the point of production, not retrofitted
pros.example: a vet-band answer leading with estimate-not-actual, its per-DVM method, source and confidence

cons.claim: A strict honesty rule can frustrate a user who wants a single confident dollar figure
cons.example: a stakeholder pressing for Lander's actual revenue and receiving only a labeled band

failure_modes: letting a band circulate without its label and confidence
answering an actual-revenue request with a point figure instead of refusing and labeling
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure in any output carries the estimate-not-actual label, its method, a public source and a confidence, and an actual-revenue request is refused with a labeled alternative
revisit_triggers: a public sales-tax or financial disclosure becomes available for a named business
a benchmark source is revised
the honesty charter is challenged or relaxed

base.update_signal: a public financial disclosure or a change to the honesty charter occurs

nodes.definition: Explain the binding cap on growing the B2B lines: scarce licensed and trained people, not customers. In veterinary the truly binding shortage is trained food-animal labor — only ~1.3% of US vets do food-animal work and rural vets average ~52 hr/week — so new large-animal practices cannot simply be willed into existence. In ag equipment the cap is CSLB-gated pump/dairy-construction trades plus a tight rural pool of pump techs, welders and electricians. Founder succession is a live concern at Sallaberry (since 1968) and TDR (since 1972). This is the reason the B2B count cannot expand to meet demand even where the herd base would support it, and it pairs with COST_STRUCTURE_BACKBONE because scarce labor is also what inflates the vet labor share to ~35-50%.

included: the ~1.3% food-animal vet share and ~52 hr/week figures
the CSLB-trade and rural skilled-labor scarcity
founder-succession risk at Sallaberry and TDR
excluded: the licensing fees themselves (in the licensing node)

pros.claim: Naming labor as the binding cap explains why demand-open B2B lines still cannot add entrants
pros.example: a herd base that would support a fourth vet practice with no food-animal DVMs available to staff it

cons.claim: Labor scarcity is a structural condition whose severity shifts with training pipelines and is hard to quantify locally
cons.example: a national vet-shortage statistic that may understate or overstate the specific Turlock food-animal pool

failure_modes: modeling B2B growth on demand alone and ignoring the people who do not exist
treating license availability as the cap when trained-labor scarcity is the real one
acceptance_tests: the cap states the ~1.3% food-animal vet share and ~52 hr/week, the CSLB-trade/rural-labor scarcity, and the founder-succession risk at the named legacy firms
revisit_triggers: a food-animal vet pipeline or licensure change
a rural skilled-trade labor-market shift
a founder-led firm approaches succession or sale

base.update_signal: a food-animal vet supply, skilled-trade pool, or succession event changes

nodes.definition: Map the capital and fleet intensity that gates format entry independent of demand: ag-equipment firms need high capex — service trucks, cranes, well rigs, welding, shop and test bench (Sallaberry pump/well, TDR dairy build); large-animal vets need moderate-to-high ambulatory trucks/vet boxes, ultrasound, lab/diagnostic gear and cold chain; feed/farm supply needs moderate warehouse, forklift, bulk bins, delivery trucks and a certified scale; music needs low-to-moderate repair bench, piano-moving gear and a rental-fleet capital pool (Hendrickson's pianos, Ingram's rentals); bike needs low-to-moderate repair stands and truing/tooling; cottage-food needs low farm-stand and dehydration gear. The mobile/dispatch lines (vets, ag equipment) trade storefront rent for fleet capex and fuel, so capex shape, not just amount, distinguishes the models.

included: the defining capex per sub-category
the mobile-fleet vs storefront-inventory capex shape
capex as a demand-independent entry gate

pros.claim: Surfacing capex intensity and shape shows why a demand-true B2B line is still hard to enter
pros.example: a well-rig-and-crane capital anchor gating pump-service entry even where dairies need the work

cons.claim: Capex varies widely by new-vs-used and project scale, so this is a relative-intensity ranking not a quote
cons.example: a used service truck and welding rig dropping ag-equipment entry cost well below a new fleet

failure_modes: judging a B2B white space on demand alone and ignoring its fleet capital anchor
treating capex as fixed when used equipment changes the entry cost materially
acceptance_tests: each sub-category's defining capex is named and the mobile-fleet vs storefront-inventory shape is identified as a demand-independent gate
revisit_triggers: equipment or fleet prices/financing change
a used-equipment opportunity changes a line's entry cost
a format adds or drops a capital-intensive capability

base.update_signal: equipment cost, financing, or a format's capability set changes

nodes.definition: Trace each line back to the dairy/almond-belt OEMs, feed mills and animal-health distributors that physically supply it, flagged as representative inference rather than confirmed contracts: ag equipment via milking-system OEMs (DeLaval, GEA, BouMatic), pump/turbine OEMs and regional dairy-supply distributors (Central Valley Dairy Supply) plus local steel/electrical wholesalers, stocking fast-moving wear parts; feed/farm supply via feed mills and nutrition cos (Purina/Land O'Lakes, Nutrena/Cargill, ADM) with cooperative buying power (Stanislaus Farm Supply through Valley Wide, a documented fact) versus dealer programs for small stores; large-animal vet via animal-health distributors (Patterson/MWI/Covetrus) and pharma with cold chain for vaccines/semen; music via instrument OEMs (Yamaha, Fender) and the school-band rental channel; bike via QBP and direct brand allocations (Raleigh, Focus, Electra, Fitbikeco); cottage-food self-produced. The dense dairy/almond economy gives short freight and direct-from-OEM dealer agreements — a genuine proximity edge — but only the Valley Wide membership and Lander's named lab divisions are documented; the rest is inference.

included: OEM, feed-mill, animal-health, instrument and bike supplier nodes per format
the inference label on supplier-to-business links
the short-freight proximity edge and the two documented exceptions

pros.claim: A format-to-supplier map shows the realistic, verified-to-serve-this-geography supply universe behind each model
pros.example: ag equipment drawing on DeLaval/GEA/BouMatic and a regional dairy-supply distributor for wear parts

cons.claim: Supplier-to-named-business links are inference and can be mistaken for confirmed contracts
cons.example: asserting Sallaberry or TDR is a specific OEM's dealer without a cited source

failure_modes: upgrading a representative supplier link to a stated fact
missing that only Valley Wide membership and Lander's lab divisions are documented
acceptance_tests: each major format has its key supplier nodes named with the inference label, and the documented Valley Wide and Lander cases are distinguished from inferred ones
revisit_triggers: a named distributor or OEM enters or exits the Valley
a documented supplier or dealer contract surfaces
a cooperative-membership change occurs

base.update_signal: a supplier relationship, OEM affiliation, or documented link changes

nodes.definition: Encode the second honesty rule as its own node: supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship. These independents do not publish vendor lists, so named distributors and OEMs are the realistic supply universe, not evidenced contracts. Only two links are documented structural facts — Stanislaus Farm Supply's membership in Valley Wide Cooperative, and Lander Veterinary's named lab divisions (Quality Milk Service, Dairy Diagnostics, OPU/Embryo Transfer). Every other supplier attribution, including specific OEM dealer affiliations for Sallaberry or TDR, is labeled inference and must never harden into an asserted contract.

included: the representative-inference label on supplier links
the two documented exceptions (Valley Wide, Lander divisions)
the no-hardening rule

pros.claim: A dedicated honesty node keeps every supplier link labeled inference from the outset and prevents quiet hardening into fact
pros.example: an OEM-affiliation answer for TDR flagged inference rather than asserted as a dealer contract

cons.claim: Strict inference labeling can read as evasive when a link is highly likely on regional norms
cons.example: a near-certain regional OEM relationship still labeled inference for want of a cited source

failure_modes: asserting a specific supplier contract without a source
losing track of which two links are actually documented
acceptance_tests: every supplier-to-business link is labeled representative inference except the documented Valley Wide and Lander cases, which are flagged as facts
revisit_triggers: a documented supplier contract surfaces for a named business
a new structural supply fact is published
the inference standard is challenged

base.update_signal: a documented supplier link or the inference standard changes

nodes.definition: Establish the licensing gates that materially raise new-entry cost across the sector, all cited facts. Pump/well and dairy construction (Sallaberry, TDR) require CSLB C-57 Well Drilling (when labor+materials exceed $500), commonly paired with C-61/D-21 Machinery & Pumps and general/structural classes for parlor builds, plus contractor bond, workers comp and commercial fleet insurance. Veterinary (Azores, Lander, Mid Valley) requires Veterinary Medical Board premises registration, DVM/RVT licensure, VACSP permits and per-premises DEA registration, with the Veterinary Medicine Mobility Act allowing field-carried controlled substances under the base DEA number; an in-person exam/valid VCPR is required to prescribe. Feed/Farm Supply requires CDFA commercial feed/fertilizer licensing and tonnage tax, DPR/County Ag Commissioner pesticide permits and scale certification. Cottage-Food (Cipponeri) falls under the CA Cottage Food Law with Class A (~$86,206) and Class B (~$172,411) gross caps on the processed slice. The binding gate differs by line: CSLB+labor for equipment, VMB+DEA+scarce-DVM for vets, CDFA for feed, CFO cap for cottage-food.

included: CSLB C-57/C-61 pump/construction gates
VMB premises + DEA mobility + VCPR vet gates
CDFA feed/fertilizer licensing
CFO Class A/B caps
the binding gate per line

pros.claim: Stating the licensing gate per line shows why the B2B count cannot simply expand to meet demand
pros.example: a would-be pump firm needing a C-57 plus bond and a CSLB-licensed crew before billing any dairy

cons.claim: Fee and class details shift, so a specific cap or class is a year-stamped figure not a permanent constant
cons.example: the CFO caps being 2025 inflation-adjusted values that move annually

failure_modes: budgeting a B2B entry without the contractor/vet licensing stack
applying the CFO cap to honey/whole produce that fall outside the statute
acceptance_tests: each line states its concrete licensing gate (CSLB, VMB/DEA, CDFA, CFO) with a public source and identifies the binding gate for that format
revisit_triggers: a CSLB, VMB, CDFA or CFO fee/requirement changes
a CFO cap is re-indexed for inflation
a new licensing class affects a line's entry

base.update_signal: a CSLB/VMB/CDFA/CFO fee or requirement changes

nodes.definition: Model the Ag Equipment & Repair line (Sallaberry Pump Service, the pump/well specialist since 1968; TDR, full dairy design/construction/equipment since 1972, the capital-projects high end; The Dairy Solutions Group, lighter-footprint dairy-profitability products). It is an owner-led skilled-trade plus capital-projects model: founder-led W-2 crews (pump techs, welders, electricians, PMs) and revenue blending parts margin, billed service labor and capital projects, dispatch- and project-driven rather than storefront. Cost structure is parts ~40-55% on service (higher on projects), trades labor ~25-35%, net ~8-15% (all estimate). It benchmarks ~$0.5M-$5M+ per operator (estimate-not-actual, low confidence) — the widest, lowest-confidence band in the sector because a parlor build dwarfs a pump repair. Entry is gated by CSLB licensing and the scarce rural skilled-trade pool, and it reads as white-space-adjacent against the county dairy capital-equipment cycle.

included: pump/service vs capital-projects mix
parts+service+project revenue and the wide band
the CSLB and skilled-labor gates and white-space-adjacent read

pros.claim: The model shows why the band is the widest in the sector and ties it to the project mix and the licensing/labor gate
pros.example: TDR's full dairy build sitting at the high end while a Sallaberry pump repair sits at the low end of one band

cons.claim: Project-mix volatility makes the revenue band the least reliable, so confidence stays low
cons.example: a year heavy on capital builds versus a year of pump repairs swinging the band enormously

failure_modes: reading the wide band as a precise figure for any one firm
modeling entry without the CSLB licensing and skilled-crew requirement
acceptance_tests: the model states the parts/service/project revenue mix, the estimate-not-actual ~$0.5M-$5M+ band with its low-confidence rationale, and ties entry to the CSLB and labor gates
revisit_triggers: a dairy capital-equipment cycle shifts
steel/pump/OEM input costs swing
a CSLB class or skilled-labor availability changes

base.update_signal: a dairy capex cycle, input cost, or CSLB/labor condition changes

nodes.definition: Model the Feed/Farm Supply line (Stanislaus Farm Supply, cooperative-scale via Valley Wide, with an ag-equipment secondary tag; Turlock Feed and Livestock Supply, ranch/hay/tack/western-wear with service revenue from blade sharpening and leather/tack repair, plus an apparel tag; Elite Feed Store, the smaller owner-operator counter format). It is a COGS-bound commodity-volume model: counter plus warehouse plus delivery, with commodity feed structurally low-margin (~70-80% COGS, labor ~10-18%, net ~2-6%, all estimate). It benchmarks ~$0.5M-$3M per operator (estimate-not-actual, medium confidence). Survival levers are cooperative scale for buying power (Stanislaus FS via Valley Wide) or blended service/retail margin (Turlock Feed's sharpening, tack, western wear); small stores cannot match coop pricing so they differentiate on service. Read against ~132 dairies plus thousands of acres the three outlets are under-saturated, not crowded.

included: commodity-volume COGS-bound model
cooperative-scale vs small-store service differentiation
the under-saturation read against the herd base

pros.claim: The model explains how a thin-margin commodity line survives on cooperative scale or service revenue rather than feed margin
pros.example: Stanislaus FS joining Valley Wide for buying power while Turlock Feed differentiates on sharpening and tack repair

cons.claim: The thin ~2-6% net leaves small independents squeezed by both the coop and big-box chains
cons.example: an unaffiliated counter store unable to match Valley Wide pricing on bulk feed

failure_modes: modeling the line on feed margin and missing that COGS dominates
reading the city per-10k figure as saturation instead of the herd denominator
acceptance_tests: the model states the ~70-80% COGS and ~2-6% net, the cooperative-scale and service-differentiation levers, the estimate-not-actual band, and the under-saturation read against the herd base
revisit_triggers: a commodity-feed or hay price swing
a cooperative-membership or pricing change
a new feed outlet enters against the herd base

base.update_signal: a feed/hay price, cooperative pricing, or feed-outlet count changes

nodes.definition: Model the Large-Animal/Dairy Vet line (Azores Veterinary Practice, commercial-herd bovine/caprine/ovine/swine with 24/7 emergency; Lander Veterinary Clinic, the most vertically diversified, with productized divisions Quality Milk Service, Dairy Diagnostics and OPU/Embryo Transfer; Mid Valley Large Animal Service, full-service ambulatory with 24/7 emergency). It is a labor-bound professional-service model on an ambulatory basis: vets drive to herds and clinics are dispatch bases, blending professional fees (palpation/repro, herd-health, emergency) with drug/consumable markup and productized lab services. Cost structure is COGS ~25-40%, high labor ~35-50% on scarce licensed DVMs, net ~10-18% (all estimate). It benchmarks ~$0.75M-$3M per practice (~$250k-$375k per veterinarian times an estimated 2-6 DVMs; estimate-not-actual, medium). High gross does not mean high net, and the band hinges on the unknown DVM count per practice, which is the named confirmation path.

included: ambulatory dispatch model and 24/7 emergency
high licensed-DVM labor share and productized lab divisions
per-vet benchmark scaled by DVM count and the high-gross-thin-net caveat

pros.claim: The model ties the high labor share to scarce licensed DVMs and shows how productized divisions lift the band
pros.example: Lander's Quality Milk Service and OPU/Embryo Transfer divisions adding revenue above plain ambulatory fees

cons.claim: The band hinges on the unknown DVM count per practice, so confidence is capped at medium
cons.example: a two-DVM versus a six-DVM practice spanning the entire ~$0.75M-$3M band

failure_modes: reading high gross as high net on the labor-heavy model
stating a practice band without flagging the unknown DVM count
acceptance_tests: the model states the ambulatory model, the ~35-50% DVM labor share, the named productized divisions, the per-vet-times-DVM-count band, and the high-gross-thin-net caveat
revisit_triggers: a food-animal DVM availability or wage shift
a practice adds or drops a productized division
a milk-quality service-demand change at the herd

base.update_signal: DVM availability, a division change, or herd service demand changes

nodes.definition: Model the Music/Instruments line (Hendrickson's Turlock Music, band/orchestra instruments and pianos with sales/rental and moving over ~40 years, owning the school-band and piano channel; Dale's Guitar, the lessons-and-repair recurring-revenue model; Ingram's Music, the rental-fleet logistics model). It is a recurring-revenue retail model that survives on service and recurring channels, not new-gear sales: lessons, school-band rental fleets, piano, and repair are stickier and higher-margin than resale, and the moat is relationships Amazon and Sweetwater cannot ship. Cost structure is ~40-60% on instrument resale (far lower on lessons/repair), labor ~20-30%, net ~5-12% (all estimate). It benchmarks ~$0.25M-$0.75M per operator (estimate-not-actual, medium). It is over-indexed versus population (three stores at 0.41 per 10k) but justified by the captive school-band and CSU recurring revenue under the LEAKAGE_RULE — genuinely crowded for 73k and the most demand-fragile consumer line.

included: lessons/rental/repair recurring channels
the resale-vs-service margin split and rental-fleet capex
the over-indexed-but-justified saturation read

pros.claim: The model shows how three stores coexist by each owning a defensible recurring channel rather than competing on resale
pros.example: Hendrickson's school-band+piano, Dale's lessons/repair and Ingram's rental fleet dividing the recurring market

cons.claim: Three stores in a 73k town is genuinely crowded and the most exposed to a demand dip
cons.example: a school-band enrollment drop compressing the rental fleets all three rely on

failure_modes: modeling the line on resale and missing that recurring service carries it
reading the over-indexed count as headroom rather than a tight equilibrium
acceptance_tests: the model names the lessons/rental/repair recurring channels, the resale-vs-service margin split, the estimate-not-actual band, and the over-indexed-but-justified read tied to the leakage rule
revisit_triggers: a school-band or CSU enrollment shift
an online instrument-retail share change
a fourth music store entering or one closing

base.update_signal: school-band/CSU demand, online retail share, or the music count changes

nodes.definition: Model the Bike Shop line (Cycle Masters, bike sales and service since 1978, carrying Raleigh/Focus/Electra/Fitbikeco and bundling free tire changes and maintenance to drive traffic). It is a service-anchored single-store model: owner-operator plus part-time help where service and recurring revenue, not boxed-goods sales, are the survival driver because the price-comparable new-bike dollar leaks online. Cost structure is goods ~50-60% (NBDA ~49.7% gross on goods, ~43% apparel), labor ~15-25%, net ~5-10% (all estimate). It benchmarks ~$0.3M-$0.8M (estimate-not-actual, medium). It sits at a one-store equilibrium with no obvious room for a second: the category is nationally contracting (~6,195 to ~3,600 US shops 2000-2022) and Modesto/online leakage caps it, so one independent shop (0.14 per 10k versus a ~0.11-per-10k US norm) is the at-market equilibrium, and service/urgency/fit is the only durable lever.

included: service-anchored single-store model
the contracting-category one-store equilibrium
the service/urgency/fit survival lever

pros.claim: The model identifies service as the survival lever where price-comparable goods leak online
pros.example: Cycle Masters bundling free tire changes and maintenance to hold the urgent/serviced dollar locally

cons.claim: A nationally contracting category caps upside even for the lone surviving shop
cons.example: a shrinking US bike-shop count holding Turlock at one store with no room for a second

failure_modes: proposing a second bike shop into a one-store equilibrium
modeling the shop on new-bike sales and ignoring the service margin
acceptance_tests: the model states the service-anchored model, the contracting-category one-store equilibrium, the estimate-not-actual band, and the service/fit survival lever
revisit_triggers: a national bike-shop count or e-bike trend shift
a Modesto/online retail change
a second shop being proposed

base.update_signal: the national bike category, online share, or local bike count changes

nodes.definition: Model the Cottage-Food/Farm Stand line (Cipponeri Family Farms, local honey, dried fruits and fresh peaches/nectarines/pluots via farm stand and pickup, with a specialty-produce secondary tag). It is a self-supplied seasonal producer model: owner/family labor selling direct, where labor and harvest timing, not distributors, govern throughput. It benchmarks <$50k-$150k (estimate-not-actual, low confidence). The format is structurally capped, not demand-capped: the CA Cottage Food Law caps gross sales and product scope on the processed slice (~$86,206 Class A / ~$172,411 Class B), but honey and whole produce fall outside CFO entirely, so only the dried/value-added line is CFO-ceilinged. The stand as a whole is therefore seasonality- and harvest-limited rather than strictly statute-limited, with a sharp summer stone-fruit window and a shelf-stable honey/dried-fruit shoulder.

included: self-supplied seasonal producer model
the CFO cap on the processed slice only
honey/whole produce outside CFO and the seasonality limit

pros.claim: The model corrects the common error of applying the CFO cap to the whole business when only the processed slice is capped
pros.example: Cipponeri's honey and whole stone fruit selling outside CFO while only the dried line is ceilinged

cons.claim: Sharp stone-fruit seasonality makes the annual band the least reliable and demands harvest-window planning
cons.example: a summer peach window carrying a disproportionate share an annual band averages away

failure_modes: applying the CFO cap to honey/whole produce outside the statute
modeling the stand on a flat annual band and missing the harvest concentration
acceptance_tests: the model states the self-supplied seasonal model, the CFO cap on the processed slice only, the honey/whole-produce CFO exclusion, and the estimate-not-actual band
revisit_triggers: a CFO cap re-indexing
a stone-fruit or honey yield/season shift
a new cottage-food micro-producer entering below the visibility threshold

base.update_signal: a CFO cap, harvest yield/season, or micro-producer count changes

nodes.definition: Synthesize the per-format saturation read against the correct denominator that explains why 14 is the equilibrium. Tightly matched to the herd base, not residents: Large-Animal/Dairy Vet (3, ~44 dairies per practice, a working ratio not oversupply). Under-saturated against the right denominator: Feed/Farm Supply (3, thin against ~132 dairies plus acreage) and Ag Equipment & Repair (3, white-space-adjacent on capital-equipment cycles). At-market on the consumer edge: Bike Shop (1, the national one-store norm). Over-indexed versus population but justified by demand drivers: Music/Instruments (3, on school-band/CSU recurring revenue, genuinely crowded). Structurally capped, not demand-capped: Cottage-Food/Farm Stand (1, CFO-limited on the processed slice). The count is herd-pulled up by the dairy/almond base and gate-pinned in place by licensing, scarce labor, supply/capital access and consumer-demand thinness with leakage.

included: per-format saturation reads against the correct denominator
the herd-pulled-up gate-pinned-in-place explanation
the under-saturated vs at-market vs over-indexed labels
excluded: the merged go/no-go verdict (that is the entry node)

pros.claim: The synthesis turns the denominator rule into an actionable per-format saturation map
pros.example: labeling feed under-saturated against the herd while bike is at-market against residents

cons.claim: B2B saturation reads are medium confidence because the herd/acre denominator is harder to size than population
cons.example: an under-saturation call that a precise herd-load-per-outlet measurement could revise

failure_modes: reading the city per-10k as saturation for a herd-scaled line
treating an under-saturated B2B line as enterable without the gate
acceptance_tests: each of the six sub-categories gets a saturation read against its correct denominator and the herd-pulled-up/gate-pinned explanation is stated
revisit_triggers: a herd/acre re-count
a format's count changes via an opening or closure
a denominator challenge on a B2B read

base.update_signal: a format count, herd/acre measure, or demand-base figure changes

nodes.definition: Encode the dominant sector risk that the whole B2B half is a derivative bet on Stanislaus County dairy plus almond cash flow. A milk-price downturn or herd shock compresses vet, equipment and feed demand simultaneously — correlated, not diversified, risk across four of six sub-categories. The 2024 avian-influenza quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies and the 2024 ~6% county ag-value decline are concrete examples of exactly this kind of upstream shock (both year-stamped 2024 facts, not restated as a live 2026 condition). Diversifying an investment across vet, feed and equipment is therefore correlated, not diversified, exposure, and the principal forward risk for the spine: when the herd contracts, all three lines contract together. The consumer edge faces a different, uncorrelated risk (category contraction and leakage).

included: the correlated-not-diversified B2B exposure
the 2024 avian-flu and ag-value-decline examples year-stamped
the consumer-edge's separate uncorrelated risk

pros.claim: Naming the correlation prevents reading a vet+feed+equipment portfolio as diversified when it is one dairy-cycle bet
pros.example: the 2024 avian-flu quarantine compressing four sub-categories at once

cons.claim: Concrete shock examples are year-stamped and must not be restated as a live condition
cons.example: treating the 2024 quarantine as a current 2026 state rather than a past illustrative shock

failure_modes: treating B2B diversification as risk reduction when it is correlated exposure
restating a 2024 shock as a current 2026 condition
acceptance_tests: the risk states the correlated B2B exposure across four sub-categories, the year-stamped 2024 examples, and the separate consumer-edge risk
revisit_triggers: a milk- or almond-price cycle moves
a new herd-health or quarantine event
a county ag-value swing

base.update_signal: a milk/almond price, herd-health event, or county ag-value figure changes

nodes.definition: Encode the coverage honesty rule that the verified count of 14 independents is a floor, not a ceiling. It is the minimum set of independent Ag & Specialty operators confirmed via public sources (business sites, Yelp/Yellowpages, Turlock Journal), not a claim of completeness. Additional micro-producers — especially cottage-food/farm-stand operators and very small feed/tack shops — plausibly exist below the visibility threshold of public listings and would only raise the count. Counts use primary category as the spine, so the straddles (Stanislaus Farm Supply's ag-equipment secondary tag, Turlock Feed's apparel tag) make the clean 3/3/3/3/1/1 split fuzzier at the edges, though saturation reads are unaffected. Source confidence also varies by business (Sallaberry, Dairy Solutions Group, Stanislaus FS, Cipponeri and Ingram's rest on medium-confidence aggregator listings).

included: the 14-count-as-floor rule
the straddle fuzziness on the primary-category spine
the per-business source-confidence variation

pros.claim: Stating coverage as a floor prevents over-claiming completeness and keeps the count honest
pros.example: flagging that uncounted micro-producers would only raise, never lower, the 14

cons.claim: A floor count complicates clean per-10k saturation math that assumes a complete denominator
cons.example: an under-counted cottage-food slice making its true density higher than listed

failure_modes: presenting 14 as a complete census rather than a verified floor
ignoring that the straddles blur the clean category split
acceptance_tests: the rule states the 14-count-as-floor status, the straddle fuzziness on the primary-category spine, and the per-business source-confidence variation
revisit_triggers: a new independent is verified via public sources
a straddle business reclassifies its primary category
a source-confidence upgrade for a listed business

base.update_signal: a verified-count change, a reclassification, or a source-confidence upgrade occurs

nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go verdict on entering or running a given Ag & Specialty format, the synthesis the whole KB builds toward. It intersects three lenses: demand against the correct denominator (SATURATION_WHITESPACE), the cost/licensing gate (REGULATORY_LICENSING_GATES, LABOR_SCARCITY_CAP, CAPEX_FLEET_INTENSITY), and the margin reality (COST_STRUCTURE_BACKBONE). The reconciled rule splits cleanly: the B2B lines are demand-open but gate-locked — feed and equipment have headroom against the herd base, but entry needs capital, OEM/distributor access and CSLB-licensed skilled trades, and for vets the binding scarcity is trained food-animal DVMs (you compete for people, not customers); the consumer lines are gate-open but demand-locked — a bike or music shop is cheap to open but demand is thin, contracting and leakage-prone, so survival requires owning a captive recurring channel from day one. Cottage-food's processed slice is statute-ceilinged, so structure around honey/whole produce for headroom. A white space that is demand-true but gate-locked is a no-go until the gate is cleared.

included: the three-lens go/no-go intersection
the demand-open-gate-locked vs gate-open-demand-locked split
the captive-recurring-channel and cottage-food structuring conditions
excluded: the underlying saturation or licensing detail (their own nodes)

pros.claim: The merged verdict prevents acting on demand headroom while ignoring the licensing/labor gate
pros.example: ruling a feed or equipment entry a no-go until OEM access and CSLB-licensed trades are secured

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a format whose demand, cost and labor point in different directions
cons.example: a feed line with real herd-base headroom but no cooperative-pricing parity needing nuance beyond go/no-go

failure_modes: issuing a go on demand alone without confirming the gate is clearable
treating B2B diversification as risk reduction when the correlated-herd lens says otherwise
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a format states the saturation read, the binding licensing/labor/capex gate, the margin reality, and the demand-open-gate-locked vs gate-open-demand-locked call
revisit_triggers: a saturation read changes
a licensing fee, labor-pool or capex condition moves
a herd-cycle shift reorders the correlated-risk picture

base.update_signal: a saturation read, cost/licensing gate, or herd-risk shift changes a format verdict

conflict_axes.name: herd_denominator_vs_resident_denominator
conflict_axes.description: B2B saturation must be read against the county herd/acre base while the consumer edge is read against city residents; a format read can apply the wrong denominator.
poles: read against the county herd/acre base
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the herd/acre denominator for ag equipment, feed and vet, and the per-resident denominator only for bike and music

conflict_axes.name: demand_open_vs_gate_locked
conflict_axes.description: The B2B lines have demand headroom against the herd base but are locked by licensing, scarce labor and capital, so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter where the herd base has room
enter only where the licensing/labor gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-open B2B line as a no-go until the CSLB/VMB/capital/labor gate is shown clearable

conflict_axes.name: gate_open_vs_demand_locked
conflict_axes.description: The consumer lines are cheap and easy to license but demand is thin, contracting and leakage-prone, so easy entry is not the same as viability.
poles: enter because the gate is cheap
enter only with a captive recurring channel
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require a captive school-band/lesson/service recurring channel from day one before entering bike or music

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-revenue B2B formats (vet, ag equipment, feed) can post strong gross while netting single digits, so revenue must never be read as profit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its COGS/labor/net benchmark before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: labeled_estimate_vs_stated_fact
conflict_axes.description: A user may want a single confident dollar figure while the honesty rule permits only a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual-revenue claim.
poles: give only a labeled estimate with confidence
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: refuse an actual-revenue claim and provide a labeled estimate with method, source, confidence and a confirmation path

conflict_axes.name: cooperative_scale_vs_independent_service
conflict_axes.description: A feed retailer can chase cooperative buying power for COGS parity or differentiate on service margin; the scale-versus-service trade.
poles: join a cooperative for buying power
differentiate on service and blended retail
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use cooperative scale where commodity volume dominates and service differentiation where the small-store counter format cannot match coop pricing

conflict_axes.name: project_mix_vs_band_precision
conflict_axes.description: The ag-equipment band is the widest because a parlor build dwarfs a pump repair, so project mix trades against any precise revenue read.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the ag-equipment band wide and low-confidence and label the project-mix swing rather than forcing a point figure

conflict_axes.name: correlated_b2b_vs_diversification_illusion
conflict_axes.description: Spreading an investment across vet, feed and equipment looks like diversification but is one correlated dairy-cycle bet.
poles: treat B2B spread as correlated exposure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model vet/feed/equipment demand as correlated to the dairy cycle, not as independent risks that diversify away

conflict_axes.name: cfo_cap_vs_outside_statute_headroom
conflict_axes.description: The CFO cap ceilings the processed slice while honey and whole produce fall outside the statute, so the cap binds only part of the stand.
poles: apply the CFO cap to the whole business
apply it only to the processed slice
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bound only the dried/value-added line with the CFO cap and treat honey/whole produce as outside-statute headroom

edge_cases.description: A milk-price downturn or herd shock compresses vet, equipment and feed demand at once
edge_cases.trigger: a dairy-cycle shock such as the 2024 avian-influenza quarantine of >110 of 132 dairies
edge_cases.mitigation: model the B2B lines as correlated to the dairy cycle, not as a diversified portfolio, and stress-test against a herd shock

edge_cases.description: A demand-open B2B line is treated as enterable while a licensing or labor gate blocks it
edge_cases.trigger: a feed or equipment headroom call ignores OEM access, capital and CSLB-licensed trades
edge_cases.mitigation: run every B2B white space through the licensing, capital and labor gate before issuing a go verdict

edge_cases.description: A new large-animal vet practice is planned with no trained food-animal DVMs available to staff it
edge_cases.trigger: a vet entry is modeled on herd demand alone against the ~1.3% food-animal vet pool
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm food-animal DVM availability before treating the herd-base headroom as enterable

edge_cases.description: A pump/dairy-construction firm is launched without the CSLB licensing stack
edge_cases.trigger: a would-be equipment entrant budgets a crew but no C-57/C-61, bond or commercial fleet insurance
edge_cases.mitigation: secure the CSLB classes, bond and fleet insurance before bidding any dairy work

edge_cases.description: The ag-equipment band is reported as a precise figure despite project-mix volatility
edge_cases.trigger: a parlor-build-heavy year is treated as a typical revenue level for a pump-service firm
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the band wide and low-confidence and label the project-mix swing rather than forcing a point figure

edge_cases.description: A feed independent without cooperative scale is squeezed on commodity margin
edge_cases.trigger: a small counter store cannot match Valley Wide pricing on bulk feed
edge_cases.mitigation: differentiate on service revenue (sharpening, tack, western wear) where coop pricing cannot be matched

edge_cases.description: A named business's revenue is requested or asserted as an actual figure
edge_cases.trigger: a question demands the real sales of a specific Turlock vet, equipment or feed firm
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to state actual revenue and provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts Sallaberry or TDR is a specific OEM's dealer without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier links labeled representative inference except the documented Valley Wide and Lander cases

edge_cases.description: The CFO cap is applied to honey and whole produce that fall outside the statute
edge_cases.trigger: the processed-slice ceiling is read as the whole farm-stand revenue cap
edge_cases.mitigation: bound only the dried/value-added line with the CFO cap and treat honey/whole produce as outside-statute headroom

edge_cases.description: A 2024 herd shock is restated as a current 2026 condition
edge_cases.trigger: the avian-influenza quarantine or the ~6% ag-value decline is presented as live
edge_cases.mitigation: year-stamp the 2024 shocks as past illustrative events and do not restate them as current 2026 conditions

edge_cases.description: The 14-business count is presented as a complete census rather than a verified floor
edge_cases.trigger: the count is used as a fixed denominator assuming completeness
edge_cases.mitigation: treat 14 as a floor that uncounted micro-producers would only raise, and flag the straddle fuzziness

workflow.action: Split the sector into its two economies
workflow.description: Assign each of the six sub-categories to the B2B spine or the consumer edge with its demand unit and payment model
workflow.gate: each sub-category is assigned to Economy A or B with its demand unit and payment model stated

workflow.action: Size the county ag base and demand expander
workflow.description: State the ~$3.15B county ag value, ~132-dairy count and the ~44-dairies-per-vet derivation as year-stamped cited facts
workflow.gate: the county value, dairy count and per-vet derivation are stated with sources and year stamps

workflow.action: Fix the correct saturation denominator per line
workflow.description: Set the herd/acre denominator for the B2B lines and the per-resident denominator for the consumer edge
workflow.gate: the herd/acre and per-resident denominators are assigned to the correct lines with the worked per-10k example

workflow.description: State the shippable-leaks vs serviced-stays rule and the bike/music equilibria
workflow.gate: Modesto/online leakage is stated and applied to the bike one-store and music recurring equilibria

workflow.description: State COGS/labor/net benchmarks by sub-category with sources as planning priors
workflow.gate: COGS, labor and net ranges are stated per sub-category as cited planning priors

workflow.action: Set the labeled-estimate revenue method and honesty rule
workflow.description: Define benchmark-times-size-signal banding with the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence, a size signal and a confirmation path

workflow.action: Establish the labor, capex and supply gates
workflow.description: State the scarce food-animal DVM and rural-trade cap, the per-format capex shape and the inference-labeled supplier map
workflow.gate: the labor scarcity cap, capex intensity and inference-labeled supplier map are stated per line

workflow.action: Establish the licensing gates per format
workflow.description: State the CSLB, VMB/DEA, CDFA and CFO gates and the binding gate per line
workflow.gate: each line states its CSLB/VMB/CDFA/CFO gate with a source and its binding gate

workflow.action: Model the B2B spine unit economics
workflow.description: For ag equipment, feed and vet, state the model, cost center, band and the gate or lever that decides viability
workflow.gate: each B2B line names its cost center, labeled band and the licensing/labor gate that decides viability

workflow.description: For music, bike and cottage-food, state the recurring/service or self-supplied model, the band and the leakage/CFO condition
workflow.gate: each consumer-edge line names its recurring/service model, labeled band and the leakage or CFO condition

workflow.action: Synthesize saturation and issue the merged go/no-go
workflow.description: Compose the per-format saturation read, the licensing/labor/capex gate and the correlated-herd risk into a demand-open-gate-locked vs gate-open-demand-locked verdict
workflow.gate: the verdict states the saturation read, binding gate, margin reality and the correct entry call per format

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or sub-category
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with method, source and confidence, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The correct denominator dominates the headline per-10k read
dominance_rules.rationale: city per-capita is the wrong measure for herd-scaled B2B lines
dominance_rules.trigger: a B2B saturation read uses city residents
dominance_rules.action: re-read the line against the county herd/acre base before judging saturation

dominance_rules.rule: The licensing/labor gate dominates demand headroom for B2B entry
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-open B2B line that cannot clear CSLB/VMB licensing or staff scarce labor is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation for a B2B line rests on herd demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the licensing and labor gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: A captive recurring channel dominates the cheap-entry illusion for consumer lines
dominance_rules.rationale: thin, contracting, leakage-prone consumer demand sinks a shop without a recurring moat
dominance_rules.trigger: a bike or music entry rests on low licensing cost
dominance_rules.action: require a captive school-band/lesson/service channel before treating the entry as viable

dominance_rules.rule: Net margin dominates gross revenue in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross B2B formats still net only single digits, so revenue must not be read as profit
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its COGS/labor/net benchmark before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The correlated-herd lens dominates the B2B diversification illusion
dominance_rules.rationale: vet, feed and equipment all derive from the same dairy cycle and contract together
dominance_rules.trigger: a B2B portfolio is treated as diversified risk
dominance_rules.action: model the spread as correlated dairy-cycle exposure, not diversification

dominance_rules.rule: Documented links dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: only Valley Wide membership and Lander's lab divisions are evidenced; the rest is inference
dominance_rules.action: label it representative inference unless it is one of the two documented cases

dominance_rules.rule: The processed-slice scope dominates the whole-business CFO-cap reading
dominance_rules.rationale: honey and whole produce fall outside the Cottage Food statute
dominance_rules.trigger: the CFO cap is applied to the entire farm stand
dominance_rules.action: bound only the dried/value-added line with the cap and treat honey/whole produce as outside-statute

dominance_rules.rule: The year stamp dominates a restated shock
dominance_rules.rationale: the 2024 herd shocks are past illustrative events, not a live 2026 condition
dominance_rules.trigger: a 2024 quarantine or ag-value decline is restated as current
dominance_rules.action: year-stamp the shock and present it as a past example, not a current state

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the herd/acre versus per-resident denominator before reading any saturation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a B2B line being mislabeled saturated on a city per-capita read that must later be reversed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a B2B white space through the licensing, capital and labor gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-open but gate-locked line and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm food-animal DVM availability before treating vet herd-headroom as enterable
anti_rework_rules.prevents: planning a vet practice that cannot be staffed from the ~1.3% food-animal pool

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every revenue band with its net benchmark in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross B2B format being approved before the thin net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the ag-equipment band wide and label the project-mix swing from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: anchoring on a precise ag-equipment figure that project volatility immediately breaks

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred OEM-dealer link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Year-stamp the 2024 herd shocks when first cited
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a past quarantine being read as a live condition and having to be walked back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat the 14-count as a floor whenever it is quoted
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a completeness claim that an uncounted micro-producer would falsify

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Stanislaus County Crop Report refresh changes the county ag value, dairy count or commodity mix
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the demand base and re-derive the per-vet ratio and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a DVM count, division count or other size signal becomes confirmable for a named practice
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue band with a tighter estimate and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a milk- or almond-price cycle or a herd-health event moves the dairy base
iteration_protocol.action: update the correlated-herd risk and the affected B2B format cost centers

iteration_protocol.trigger: a CSLB, Veterinary Medical Board, CDFA or Cottage-Food fee or requirement changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the licensing gate and any format whose entry the change affects

iteration_protocol.trigger: a food-animal DVM pipeline or rural skilled-trade labor-market shift occurs
iteration_protocol.action: update the labor-scarcity cap and the vet and equipment growth reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a documented supplier or OEM-dealer contract surfaces for a named business
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the affected supplier link from inference to fact and update the supply map

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes or a new independent is verified, changing a per-format count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read, the coverage floor and the merged go/no-go for that format

iteration_protocol.trigger: an online or Modesto big-box retail change shifts consumer-edge leakage
iteration_protocol.action: update the leakage rule and the bike and music equilibria

priority_rationale: The two-economy split, the county ag base, the herd/acre denominator and the leakage rule come first because every format judgment depends on placing the format in the right economy and reading its demand against the right unit; the cost-structure backbone, labeled-estimate method and its honesty rule, the labor/capex/supply inputs and the licensing gates come next because they are the lenses that turn demand into unit economics and decide enterability independent of demand; the six format models then apply all of that to the concrete Turlock businesses; and the saturation synthesis, correlated-herd risk, coverage floor and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict.
